title: Oracle bone inscriptions
description: Diviners of the Shang kings carve questions on bones and turtle shells, the earliest substantial body of Chinese writing.

title: Battle of Muye
description: King Wu of Zhou defeats the Shang, founding the longest-lasting Chinese dynasty.

title: Birth of Confucius
description: The teacher whose ideas on duty, family and government shape Chinese society for two and a half thousand years is born in the state of Lu.

title: Battle of Changping
description: Qin destroys the army of Zhao, clearing the way for its conquest of the other states.

title: Qin unification
description: The state of Qin conquers its last rival and its king takes the title of First Emperor.

title: Han dynasty founded
description: Liu Bang becomes emperor; the Han rule, with one interruption, for four centuries.

title: Zhang Qian sets out for the west
description: Emperor Wu's envoy travels to Central Asia, and his reports open the routes later called the Silk Road.

title: Cai Lun presents papermaking
description: The court official is credited with the method of making paper from bark, hemp and rags.

title: Battle of Red Cliffs
description: Cao Cao's southward advance is defeated; the exact site is disputed.

title: End of the Han dynasty
description: Cao Pi forces the last Han emperor to abdicate, and China divides into the Three Kingdoms.

title: Battle of Fei River
description: The Eastern Jin defeat a much larger northern army, keeping the south independent.

title: Sui reunifies China
description: The Sui conquer the Chen dynasty in the south, ending nearly three centuries of division.

title: Tang dynasty founded
description: Li Yuan takes the throne after the fall of the Sui.

title: Battle of Talas
description: An Abbasid army defeats the Tang, marking the limit of Chinese expansion into Central Asia.

title: An Lushan rebellion begins
description: A frontier general's revolt starts eight years of war that permanently weaken the Tang.

title: Diamond Sutra printed
description: A woodblock scroll found at Dunhuang is the oldest dated printed book.

title: Song dynasty founded
description: Zhao Kuangyin is made emperor by his troops and reunifies most of China.

title: Fall of Kaifeng
description: The Jurchen Jin capture the Song capital and two emperors, and the Song court moves south.

title: Yuan dynasty proclaimed
description: Kublai Khan gives his realm a Chinese dynastic name.

title: Battle of Yamen
description: The last Song fleet is destroyed and the Mongol conquest of China is complete.

title: Ming dynasty founded
description: Zhu Yuanzhang proclaims the Ming and drives the Yuan court north later that year.

title: Zheng He's first voyage
description: The first of seven treasure-fleet expeditions sets out across the Indian Ocean.

title: Capital moved to Beijing
description: The Yongle Emperor moves the Ming capital to Beijing, where the Forbidden City has just been completed.

title: Portuguese settle at Macau
description: Ming officials allow Portuguese traders a permanent base, the first European settlement in China.

title: Battle of Shanhai Pass
description: Manchu forces pass the Great Wall and go on to take Beijing; Qing rule over China begins.

title: Treaty of Nerchinsk
description: The Qing and Russia fix their border in the first treaty between China and a European power.

title: Macartney embassy
description: The Qianlong Emperor receives Britain's envoy and refuses his requests for wider trade.

title: Destruction of opium at Humen
description: Commissioner Lin Zexu destroys more than a thousand tons of confiscated British opium, the trigger for the First Opium War.

title: Treaty of Nanjing
description: Ends the First Opium War, ceding Hong Kong Island and opening treaty ports.

title: Taiping Rebellion begins
description: Hong Xiuquan proclaims the Heavenly Kingdom; the civil war that follows kills at least twenty million people.

title: Old Summer Palace burned
description: British troops destroy the imperial gardens at the end of the Second Opium War.

title: Allied armies take Beijing
description: Troops of eight nations relieve the foreign legations besieged during the Boxer Uprising, and the court flees.

title: Wuchang Uprising
description: An army mutiny sets off the revolution that ends the Qing dynasty.

title: Republic of China founded
description: Sun Yat-sen is inaugurated provisional president, and the last emperor abdicates six weeks later.

title: May Fourth Movement
description: Student protests against the Versailles settlement grow into a wider cultural and political movement.

title: Chinese Communist Party founded
description: Thirteen delegates hold the party's first congress in the French Concession.

title: Shanghai massacre
description: Chiang Kai-shek turns on his Communist allies, beginning the civil war between the two parties.

title: Long March begins
description: The Red Army breaks out of its encircled base and retreats for a year to the north-west, during which Mao Zedong becomes its leader.

title: Marco Polo Bridge incident
description: A clash between Chinese and Japanese troops opens full-scale war.

title: Nanjing Massacre
description: Japanese troops take the capital and over six weeks kill great numbers of civilians and prisoners.

title: People's Republic proclaimed
description: Mao Zedong announces the founding of the People's Republic of China.

title: Great Leap Forward
description: A campaign of forced collectivisation and backyard industry leads to a famine that kills tens of millions.

title: First nuclear test
description: China explodes its first atomic bomb.

title: Cultural Revolution begins
description: A party circular drafted under Mao launches a decade of purges, Red Guard violence and upheaval.

title: Nixon visits China
description: The American president meets Mao, ending more than twenty years without relations between the two countries.

title: Tangshan earthquake
description: An earthquake levels the city and kills at least 240,000 people.

title: Death of Mao Zedong
description: Mao dies after ruling China for 27 years, and the Gang of Four are arrested a month later.

title: Reform and opening up
description: At the Third Plenum of the Central Committee, Deng Xiaoping's line of economic reform replaces class struggle as the party's priority.

title: Shenzhen Special Economic Zone
description: The first of the special economic zones of the reform era is established.

title: Tiananmen Square protests suppressed
description: The army clears weeks of student-led protests from central Beijing by force.

title: Handover of Hong Kong
description: Britain returns Hong Kong to Chinese sovereignty.

title: China joins the World Trade Organization
description: Membership after fifteen years of negotiation ties China into world trade.

title: Sichuan earthquake
description: An earthquake of magnitude 7.9 kills nearly 70,000 people.

title: Beijing Olympics
description: The Summer Olympics open in Beijing.
